subject: Bar chart with Percentages of Subpopulation

messages.author: 950b82e8be250189
messages.subject: Bar chart with Percentages of Subpopulation
parts:
Hi everyone,

I'm new to ggplot and need some help with bar graphs. Online different solutions were offered but none seemed to work for me (perhaps because they were for older versions?).

I would like N bar charts next to each other one for the each subpopulation (i.e. N =2 so a bar chart for A=0 and one for A=1). In each bar chart I want to graph the categorical variable B (say B=0, B=1) on the x-axis and the percentage of the subpopulation's total C on the y-axis.
In particular the percentages in each subgroup add up to 100% (i.e. for A=0, B=0 has 25% of the C and B=1 has 75% of the C).

The data looks like this
A  B C
0  0  75
0  1  12
0  1  12
0  1   1
1  0  33
1  1  34
1  0  33

So here I want a bar chart for group A which shows that for A=0, 75% of the total C of A=0 falls into B=0, and 25% of it fall into B=1. For A=1 we have 66% falling into B=0 and 34% falling into B=1.

Please let me know if you'd need more information to understand my problem.
Thank you very much for your help,

Sebastian

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Bar chart with Percentages of Subpopulation
parts:
Can you dput() your dataframe to make it a bit easier?

It sounds like you need to summarize across A and B to get your numbers for plotting and then plot from there. 

Brandon
